function.mechanism: Provides buffering and mineral chelation (sequestration), supports leavening systems, and helps stabilize texture/water-binding in processed foods.
common_food_categories: canned fish (specific US standard allows sodium acid pyrophosphate)

adi.basis: Group ADI for phosphates expressed as phosphorus (EFSA FAF 2019 re-evaluation).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA considered the ADI protective but estimated exposures exceeded ADI in some child groups and in supplement scenarios.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR 182.1087; 21 CFR 182.6787; 21 CFR 182.6789; 21 CFR 182.8223; see also 21 CFR 161.190 for a specific canned tuna limit
fda.notes: GRAS when used in accordance with GMP in cited sections; sodium acid pyrophosphate may be used up to 0.5% by weight in canned tuna under 21 CFR 161.190.

adi.basis: Group MTDI for phosphorus from all sources, expressed as P, applied across phosphate/diphosphate evaluations.

concerns.summary: EFSA reported modeled ADI exceedance for some younger age groups and supplement scenarios, indicating potential risk where exposure is high.

Recent reviews propose that highly absorbable inorganic phosphate additives may contribute to cardiorenal risk pathways (e.g., vascular calcification, mineral-hormone dysregulation), especially at high cumulative exposure.
US packaged-food analyses show widespread phosphate additive presence, increasing likelihood of cumulative dietary exposure from processed foods.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation reported no concern for genotoxicity and carcinogenicity for the phosphate group assessed.
EFSA reported no developmental toxicity effects in the dataset reviewed.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2019 reported exceedance of the group ADI in modeled scenarios for multiple younger populations (mean and/or 95th percentile) and for supplement exposure.

risk_assessment.rationale: E450 compounds are approved by EFSA/FDA/JECFA with defined intake guidance, but EFSA identified ADI exceedance in several younger populations and recent literature indicates plausible cardiorenal concerns at high cumulative phosphate-additive exposure.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI exists (40 mg/kg bw/day as phosphorus) and additive remains authorized
EFSA modeled ADI exceedance in child groups and supplement scenarios
JECFA group MTDI framework (70 mg/kg bw as P) supports controlled-use acceptability
Recent US market data show broad phosphate additive prevalence in packaged foods
No IARC monograph classification identified for E450-related pyrophosphate entries
